page: Amazon Web Services m8gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The physical compute configuration consists of 64 dedicated physical cores running on 64 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, utilizing the 64-bit ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture clocked at 2.8 GHz. Memory is provisioned at 256 GB, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The platform incorporates 3800 GB of directly attached NVMe SSD instance storage and supports a baseline network throughput of 30 Gbps.

Benchmark analysis reflects notable strengths in memory throughput and multi-threaded parallel computation. The server records top-tier memory read bandwidth of 464.3 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks and write speeds of 224.26 GB/sec, accompanied by a Geekbench multi-core result of 25,674 and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 654.51 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates exceptional transactional speed, logging 134.49 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations alongside 128.63 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. In contrast, single-thread synthetic benchmarks remain in the median range, with Geekbench single-core reaching 1,899 and single-threaded gzip compression registering 30.31 GB/sec.

From an architectural standpoint, the instance relies entirely on ARM64 instruction execution and native AES hardware cryptography, omitting discrete GPUs and x86 vector instructions such as AVX-512. The presence of high-speed local NVMe storage reduces external block storage overhead, delivering strong hardware-level efficiency for IO-heavy services. The absence of multi-threading per core ensures predictable, isolated compute cycles across all 64 cores without hyperthreading resource contention.

The m8gd.16xlarge is engineered for scale-out workloads requiring fast local scratch disks and intensive parallel compute. Target operational use cases include high-throughput Redis or Memcached clusters, relational database engines with direct SSD storage dependencies, large-scale software builds, batch ETL pipelines, and microservice container consolidation.
description: Amazon Web Services m8gd.16xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 64 dedicated ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz, paired with 256 GB of memory and 3800 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local storage. Operating on the AWS Nitro system with 30 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, this arm64 configuration delivers a balanced 4.0 GB RAM per core allocation. Hardware testing indicates exceptional multi-core and memory subsystem throughput, with uncached read memory bandwidth reaching 464.3 GB/sec, a Geekbench multi-core score of 25,674, and 134.49 million Redis SET operations per second. While single-thread execution aligns with mid-range baselines and x86 vector extensions are absent, the architecture yields high resource density and IOPS performance. These capabilities establish the server as a viable platform for high-concurrency database deployments, distributed caching, parallel CI/CD compilation, and enterprise container infrastructure.
